headline: On the hottest day of the summer, walkers on 69% of Milton Keynes' footpaths faced very strong heat stress.
deck: That is a feels-like temperature of 38 °C or more, for at least an hour.
sources: Environment Agency lidar flown in winter 2020–21 gives the shape of the whole area. A custom deep-learning model sorts its points into ground, buildings, trees and water. SOLWEIG (Lindberg et al. 2008) then follows the sun over those buildings and trees hour by hour on 13 August 2026 and works out the radiant heat a person takes in on each 1 m square. With each hour's air temperature, humidity, wind and sunshine from the Met Office's 2 km UKV model, that gives the feels-like temperature (UTCI). Footpaths are from OpenStreetMap and bus stops from NaPTAN; places built since the flight are greyed. New trees are placed as TreePlanter does (Wallenberg et al. 2022).

stops.name: stops
stops.label: Shade at bus stops
stops.headline: 2,175 trees and 31 shelters would spare people waiting at all 779 bus stops from very strong heat stress, not 464.
stops.deck: The average bus stop would spend no time in it, not 79 minutes. Footpaths would barely change: 69% would still reach it.
stops.note: 2,175 new trees 8 m tall, each where it shades the most of a bus stop's waiting area in the hours it is at 38 °C or more; a shelter at the 31 stops no tree could cool.

trees.name: trees
trees.label: 10% more trees
trees.headline: 10% more trees would halve the footpaths where walkers face very strong heat stress: 34%, not 69%.
trees.deck: A stretch of footpath would spend 0.5 hours in it, not 2.1, and 2% would spend 5 hours or more, not 24%. 772 of the 779 bus stops would stay out of it all day, not 464.
trees.note: 52,059 new trees 8 m tall beside the 520,586 trees and tall shrubs standing now (counted from the lidar): first the 2,175 for the bus stops, then each where its shade falls on the most sunlit footpath in the hottest hours.
